title: trigger
description: A way in. Names its kind (a document a plugin grants: an http route, a cli command, a topic...), the settings that kind's contract judges, the edge types it takes and answers, and the run node it fires: a domain port operation, with its inputs read from the kind's context. Nothing here knows what a URL is; the kind does.

$schema.description: The kind of this document: its published schema URL, or the alias @wilanis/trigger.schema.json.

description.description: What this trigger lets in and what it fires, in one or two sentences.

label.description: A short human name for this document, shown wherever a reader sees it instead of its path. Absent: the file name stands in.

kind.description: The trigger kind this trigger is of: a document a plugin grants (`@http/http.trigger-kind.json`, `@cli/cli.trigger-kind.json`). It declares the `settings` this trigger may carry and the `context` its `fire.in` and its policies read as `{{context.*}}`; `wilanis describe` on it shows both.

settings.description: The values the kind's settings contract judges. May read {{secrets.key}} and nothing else.

policies.description: The policies that gate this trigger, in order: each decides over what the kind and the guard hand as context.*, and the first that does not allow answers. An attachment gives the guard the credentials it verifies, read from the kind's context like any input: { "policy": "...", "in": { "token": "{{context.headers.authorization}}" } } -- a list is the places a credential may sit, the first present wins. A bare path attaches a policy that reads what an earlier attachment supplied. Every reason a policy can refuse with is mapped like any other (T005). Absent: the trigger is public.

in.description: credential name -> a read of the kind's context, or a list of reads (the first present wins). The names are the guard's: token, challenge.

description.description: Why this policy is attached here, for a reader of the trigger.

fire.description: What this trigger invokes: one run node. `run` names a domain port operation (path#operation) and `in` gives every value it takes, reading {{context.*}} from the kind's context. The node type is not written -- a trigger fires exactly one operation, so this schema is the declaration. A trigger never names a graph: it states what it wants done, and the port's binding decides how.

description.description: What firing this operation does, for a reader of the trigger.

label.description: A short human name for this call, shown wherever a reader sees it.
